_comment: Tracked-known reds: a non-PASS file listed here is a tracked, owned bug and does NOT gate the build. gate_verdict.py turns RED only on a NEW (unlisted) non-PASS file. When a listed file starts PASSing, remove it in the same change that confirms the fix. Built from the 2026-06-10 full-suite triage (368/369 on the 128 GB box). The periodic-gauge cluster shares one root cause: the b4a6faba merge dropped EWALD_3D gauge enforcement (a261613a F1/F3 + d316f266 force blocks) from the multi-k/GDF/open-shell drivers (62451802 / docs/pbc_audit_2026-06.md / HANDOVER_PERIODIC_GAUGE_CONSISTENCY.md). Energies for those are non-physical/over-bound (E != e_elec + e_nuc, the 0.189 decomposition gap). All periodic reds -> periodic-scf chat; relaxed_scan -> molecular-optimize/scan chat.

known_reds.ref: root-caused 2026-08-12; the 13 SCC-DFTB nodes are FIXED, the 4 listed here are separate and remain red
known_reds.reason: SHRUNK 2026-08-12 from 15 nodes to 4. Root cause of the 13 SCC-DFTB nodes was a split default, NOT the finite-temperature-retry heuristic the earlier note here blamed: 868a3357f added the SCC-DFTB DIIS charge accelerator with use_diis defaulting to true on BOTH sides, and 5535a0c78 ('restore Aitken as default') reverted only the C++ struct -- its diffstat is four C++ files. SCCDFTBModel.__init__ kept use_diis=True and dftb0.py pushes it onto SCCOptions verbatim, so Python won and every closed-shell SCC-DFTB run kept using the accelerator the revert meant to disable (USCCDFTBModel never sets the field, so open-shell was unaffected). The BUG-023 revert series (64473ca61 / 8baca59e6 / 6c40ade60 / 19c7aad9a) restored 'v0.15.116 state' faithfully -- but v0.15.116 already carried the split, and 19c7aad9a fixed only the bare run_scc_dftb() function and periodic.py, not the model constructor. Fixed by setting dftb0.py's default to False; guarded by TestSCCOptionDefaultParity in tests/test_semiempirical_dftb0.py, which pins every SCCDFTBModel keyword default against the C++ SCCOptions default. Measured on this tree: 17 failed/9 passed before, 4 failed/22 passed after. The 4 remaining are unrelated to use_diis and were verified to fail identically with and without the fix: the three test_pm6_* nodes are on the PM6/NDDO path (formamide dimer differs only in exact n_iter, 280 vs a pinned 251; the other two hit VibeQCSCFConvergenceError after a pathological optimizer step), and test_scc_dftb_hcooh_trial asserts prior_retry.converged for the T=0.0012 rung -- it was re-pinned on 2026-08-06 for a world where diis_subspace defaulted to 2, but the BUG-023 reverts restored scc_dftb.hpp:37 to 6, so that rung now exhausts 500 iterations under BOTH conventions. Fixing those four means re-pinning PM6 iteration counts on physical outcomes and re-deriving the hcooh rung expectation against the current subspace default; neither should be done by re-tuning the retry ladder (CLAUDE.md section 7).

Fixtures in these four files still use pre-hoist cutoffs and now correctly trip BipoleFoldUnreliableError (e.g. MgO/STO-3G S(Gamma) fold truncation 1.5e-2 at cutoff 10 bohr, matching the documented 1e-2 threshold and the docstring's own worked example). The same commit already updated several sibling consumer files (test_bipole_production_guards.py, test_bipole_multipole_far_field_retired.py, test_pbc_bipole_ewald_split_integration.py) to the new stricter guard; these four were missed. Non-blocking: pbc-bipole lane is classified under-review/post-cut-evaluation in suite_manifest.json (not gated pre-cut). Stable at 32 failed/115 passed across two full re-runs (pre- and post- a 33-commit landing gap), confirming this is the intentional guard behavior, not a growing regression. Fix is mechanical (bump fixture cutoff_bohr to converge below 1e-2, or update the affected fixtures the same way 6299692ae updated its sibling files) but is BIPOLE-chat territory, not release-chat. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 (BIPOLE chat): 33 failed / 114 passed; ~30 nodes remain the deterministic fold-guard refusals, 3 are warning-text drift on the far-field surface (tests match 'experimental', code warns 'RETIRED') owned by the far-field refactor work, not fixture cutoffs. Exact per-fixture re-cut cutoffs measured via fold-drift ladders (agentic-loop/bug-claims.md KNOWN-RED RE-MEASUREMENT 2026-08-12; evidence ~/.claude-fixer-runs/bipole-exact-zone/knownred-recut-2026-08-12/): H2 basin 6->8, BeH2 ->13, BeH ->11, MgO ->12, but LiH Gamma needs cutoff 18 to enter SCF, so the four LiH FD-gradient nodes are not cheap re-cuts (slow-lane budget or fixture swap).

_known_reds_resolved: 2026-06-13 (EWALD_3D retirement): tests/test_periodic_dense_ionic_energy_parity.py RESOLVED -> known_reds now EMPTY (zero tracked reds). The dense-ionic bug is fixed by FAIL-CLOSING the Gamma-only EWALD_3D drivers (CLAUDE.md 7): run_r{h,k}f_periodic_gamma_ewald3d now RAISE when the largest cross-cell AO overlap |S_mu_nu(L!=0)| exceeds ~0.3 -- a BASIS-aware molecular-limit-breakdown signal, NOT geometric -- naming jk_method=gdf(default)/bipole/gpw; the user-facing route (jk_method='fft_poisson') is retired (validate_jk_method raises). KEY re-measurement this pass (verify-first): only LiH is actually buggy. LiH overlap 0.41 -> EWALD -35.9655 vs GDF -33.9940 = 1.97 Ha (Li 2s/2p are extraordinarily diffuse, alpha=0.048). MgO (overlap 0.19, |dE|=0.1 mHa) and NaCl (0.12, <1 uHa) are FINE -- the baseline had assumed them buggy without re-running. LiH and MgO have near-identical nearest-image contact (3.86 vs 3.98 bohr) so a geometric criterion would wrongly refuse fine MgO; the overlap criterion separates them. Old <1e-3 parity assertions replaced by pytest.raises + surgical-spare guards; MgO/NaCl stay live PASS guards. Mechanics tests that need a dense cell pass allow_dense_ionic=True (internal escape hatch). --- PRIOR: 2026-06-13: tests/test_periodic_gradient_g1a.py::test_h2_box_matches_fd (the lone periodic known-red) RESOLVED. Root cause: the analytic EWALD Gamma gradient built the energy-weighted-density (overlap-Lagrangian) W from the driver's reported mo_energies, which sit on a shifted orbital-energy reference (the alpha_HF-scaled real-space exact-exchange G=0 self-image gauge; pure-DFT offset = 0). Fix: compute_gradient_periodic_rhf_gamma now rebuilds the variational Fock F_var = dE/dD from the converged density in the molecular limit and takes eps from it, so the overlap term is gauge-consistent with the SCF energy and FD (H2/STO-3G/20-A box HF: 0.1927 -> 0.1486 = FD). RKS pure-DFT unaffected (no exchange gauge); the RKS-hybrid molecular-limit gauge correction has a variational_xc_fock hook pending an SCF-grid-matched V_xc thread.

_known_slow_comment: Slow files that exceed the fast-lane timeout: NOT broken (no assertion failures at generous timeout), tracked here so they do NOT gate; run on the slow/nightly lane (generous timeout, 128 GB box). 2026-06-10 re-fast pass (this commit): the original boilerplate reason ('auto_optimize_truncation + fine grid') was DISPROVEN — auto_optimize_truncation=False is moot (45.8 vs 46.2s) and grid-spacing is irrelevant (analytic-FT J); the real cost is the per-iteration analytic-FT Hartree-J / V_ne rebuild (EWALD, forced cutoff-18 on tight cells) and GPW plane-wave-grid collocation (PBC-audit E2/E3). 10 files were de-slowed and removed from this list (DIIS for the dilute-box ewald3d drivers: test_periodic_rhf_ewald/_multi_k 17->3 iters; fixed-density proxy: test_periodic_dense_ionic_bug; @slow on the few heavy validations while keeping the fast majority: test_caspt2_rdm_factorization, test_parity_hf_dft, test_cli; plus test_periodic_symmetry/test_pw1pw/test_bipole_fock_ewald/test_bipole_gradient which already pass the fast lane). test_periodic_rhf_multi_k_ewald moved to known_reds (1 b4a6faba gauge test surfaced once fast). The 13 remaining are genuinely driver-efficiency-bound (per-iteration FT J on tight ionic cells / GPW grid collocation / GDF Lpq build) — left tracked per maintainer decision 2026-06-10 with the E2/E3 efficiency follow-up to the periodic-scf + GPW + gdf chats (docs/pbc_audit_2026-06.md). These do NOT gate. 2026-06-11: test_periodic_accelerator_uniformity.py added — the b4a6faba merge-drop restoration brought the file back from a 38-line stub to its full 24-test end-to-end form (every periodic backend x every accelerator SCF, ~700 s standalone); genuinely SCF-bound, slow-lane material. The 7 periodic gauge-cluster known_reds were removed in the same change — the merge-drop restoration (the fix the baseline _comment predicted) landed and they PASS. 2026-06-13: 7 entries flagged 'resolved' (now PASSing within the fast-lane timeout) by the 2026-06-13 fast-lane gate run were removed: test_ase_periodic_gpw, test_basis_filter, test_periodic_gapw_gradient, test_periodic_grid, test_periodic_rhf_ewald_diis, test_periodic_runner_gpw_dispatch, test_periodic_accelerator_uniformity. 2026-06-13 (gdf chat): test_pbc_gdf_compcell removed — its dominant test (test_pbc_gdf_rhf_lih_primitive_uha_parity_via_rsgdf) was split so the ke=800 µHa half is @slow and the ke=400 chem-acc guard stays in the fast lane; the non-@slow file now runs ~104s (was ~370s) after the cderi<->V_ne AO-pair-FT dedup (fee8f0ac) + the split. 6 known_slow entries remain. If a future fast-lane run TIMEOUTs any removed file it becomes a NEW red and correctly gates RED; re-add it then. 2026-06-17 (v0.13.1 cleanup): RE-ADDED test_periodic_gapw_gradient, test_periodic_accelerator_uniformity, test_ase_periodic_gpw, test_basis_filter (4 entries; list 4->8). They were wrongly de-listed 2026-06-13 - that pass removed them after a single quiet fast-lane run showed them under-timeout, but the EWALD analytic-FT J caching (PBC-audit E2) that motivated the de-slow only sped the EWALD route; it never touched GPW/GAPW plane-wave-grid collocation (the separate E3 work, NOT done) or the basis-filter memory tier. Under the v0.13.0-cut fast lane (--jobs 6, box load ~80) all four false-red'd (ABORT/TIMEOUT/OOM); all four (plus the already-listed gapw_hessian/gapw_open_shell) reconfirmed PASS in clean --jobs 1 isolation 2026-06-17 on a fresh-built core (per-file numbers in each reason), so none masks a bug. Complementary safety net: gate_verdict.py --reverify (the same v0.13.1 cleanup) re-runs any NEW *unlisted* red alone before gating, covering the lighter contention victims deliberately left off this list because they pass the fast lane in isolation (test_periodic_runner_gpw_dispatch ~408s, test_periodic_dense_ionic_energy_parity ~350s) without the masking risk of a known_slow entry.
